headline: Failed resolution would have canceled a Medicare pilot using contractors and AI tools for prior authorization in six states.
what_it_does: This resolution would have used the Congressional Review Act to cancel a July 2025 Medicare notice creating the WISeR Model. That model requires approval in advance (prior authorization) for certain services in traditional Medicare in six states: New Jersey, Ohio, Oklahoma, Texas, Arizona, and Washington. Private contractors review these requests using technology such as artificial intelligence and are paid based on a share of the savings. The resolution would have stopped CMS from continuing the model, which began on January 1, 2026.

who_it_affects.group: People with traditional Medicare in New Jersey, Ohio, Oklahoma, Texas, Arizona, and Washington
who_it_affects.how: They would no longer have needed advance approval under this model before getting certain services covered.

who_it_affects.group: Doctors, hospitals, and other Medicare providers in the six states
who_it_affects.how: They would no longer have had to submit prior authorization requests under this model for the covered services.

who_it_affects.group: Companies contracted to run the WISeR Model
who_it_affects.how: Their work reviewing requests, and their pay tied to a share of savings, would have ended.
The agency would have been barred from continuing this six-year test of the model.
